newsitem.title: UK: UK Centrica says gas levy abolition cuts costs.
newsitem.headline: UK Centrica says gas levy abolition cuts costs.

text.p: British gas supplier Centrica plc on Wednesday said UK finance minister Gordon Brown's decision to cut the gas levy to zero from April 1998 would cut company costs.
"We welcome it, yes, we're pleased, it does reduce our costs," a spokesman for the company said.
The gas levy was imposed in 1981 on eight fields in the North Sea which were not covered by the Petroleum Revenue Tax introduced in 1975. Seven of these are still producing.

The levy was originally paid only by British Gas plc as the monopoly buyer. But since its demerger into BG plc and Centrica, it is Centrica which has inherited the obligation to pay the levy. In 1996/1997, the levy produced 200 million stg, consultant Julian Kennedy at Wood Mackenzie said.
Kennedy estimated that the levy accounted for about one penny a therm of BG's Weighted Average Cost of Gas (WACOG) of around 19 to 20 pence a therm.
A reduction by this amount would help Centrica become more cost competitive with its new rivals as the gas market continues to open for competition this year and next, he said.
Combined with a cut in VAT on fuel bills and other gas price cuts already announced Brown said he expected gas prices to fall in real terms by 5.5 percent this year and 11 percent next year.

Centrica said the company was still studying what the reduction meant in terms of pricing. It was not clear if Brown's figures included the reduction in transport costs following the price control placed on pipeline operator Transco by regulator Ofgas and the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, he said.
But the spokesman added that Centrica would benefit as its costs decreased, its charges to customers will fall, and its competitiveness will increase.
